Healthy.description: The crop foliage shows vibrant green color, strong leaf tissue integrity, and no visible symptoms of fungal, bacterial, or viral infection.
possible_causes: Good air circulation and sunlight exposure

immediate_actions: Continue current crop care and irrigation schedule.
Maintain regular monitoring to catch early signs of pest or fungal pressure.
prevention: Apply balanced N-P-K fertilizer as per soil test recommendations.
Maintain clean weeding around plant bases.
Ensure proper drip or ground-level irrigation to keep foliage dry.
recommended_actions.when_to_seek_expert_help: No expert intervention required at this stage. Keep monitoring periodically.

Early Blight.description: A common fungal disease caused by Alternaria solani. It primary affects foliage, stems, and fruits, starting on older lower leaves.
symptoms: Dark brown circular spots with concentric rings ('target board' pattern)
Yellow halos surrounding brown leaf spots
Lower leaves yellowing and dropping off prematurely
possible_causes: High humidity combined with warm temperatures (24-29°C)
Spores surviving in contaminated crop debris or soil

immediate_actions: Prune and destroy heavily infected lower leaves to reduce spore count.
Avoid overhead irrigation; water directly at the plant root zone.
Mulch around the base of plants to prevent soil splash onto lower leaves.
prevention: Practice 3-4 year crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops.
Maintain adequate spacing between plants to maximize airflow.
Use bio-fungicides like Trichoderma viride or organic Copper-based sprays during early growth stages.
recommended_actions.when_to_seek_expert_help: Consult your local Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) or agriculture officer if leaf defoliation exceeds 25% of the canopy.

Late Blight.description: A destructive water-mold (oomycete) infection caused by Phytophthora infestans. It can destroy entire crops within days under cool, wet conditions.
symptoms: Large, irregular water-soaked pale green to dark brown patches on leaves
White cottony fungal growth on the undersides of leaves in humid conditions
Rapidly wilting and collapsing foliage, dark stem lesions
possible_causes: Cool, moist weather (15-22°C) with fog or relative humidity >90%
Wind-blown spores traveling from infected nearby fields
Infected seed tubers or volunteer plants nearby

immediate_actions: Isolate and remove severely infected plants immediately.
Stop all overhead watering to prevent spore dispersal.
Apply approved protective fungicides such as Mancozeb or Copper Oxychloride as recommended by local guidelines.
prevention: Ensure excellent field drainage and wide row spacing.
Destroy crop residues promptly after harvest.
recommended_actions.when_to_seek_expert_help: Immediate expert consultation recommended as Late Blight spreads rapidly and threatens neighboring fields.

Leaf Mold.description: A fungal disease caused by Passalora fulva (syn. Cladosporium fulvum), common in high humidity environments and greenhouses.
symptoms: Pale green or yellow spots on the upper leaf surface
Olive-green to velvety brown mold growth on the lower leaf surface
Infected leaves wither and drop off prematurely

immediate_actions: Improve airflow by pruning lower suckers and dense branches.
Reduce ambient humidity by widening vent openings or spacing.
Remove affected leaves carefully to avoid shaking spores into the air.
prevention: Sterilize plant stakes and trellising material between seasons.
Apply bio-agents like Bacillus subtilis as a preventative spray.
recommended_actions.when_to_seek_expert_help: Seek guidance if mold spreads to upper canopy leaves or fruit stems.

Septoria Leaf Spot.description: A fungal disease caused by Septoria lycopersici. It causes severe leaf spot and defoliation, reducing fruit yields and exposing fruit to sunscald.
symptoms: Numerous small, circular spots (2-3 mm) with dark brown borders and grey centers
Tiny black dots (pycnidia) inside the centers of mature spots
Progressive yellowing and leaf loss starting from lower foliage upward
possible_causes: Frequent rainfall or wet leaves for extended periods
Spores splashing from soil or infected debris

immediate_actions: Pick off affected lower leaves as soon as spots appear.
Apply organic mulch (straw or plastic) to prevent soil splash.
Avoid working in the field while plants are wet.
prevention: Clean equipment and stakes with mild disinfectant.
Rotate crops every 2-3 years away from nightshade family plants.
Utilize preventative copper or sulphur formulations.
recommended_actions.when_to_seek_expert_help: Consult an agricultural extension specialist if spotting spreads past mid-level branches.
